well-max-yield.formula: max_yield_gpm = specific_capacity_gpm_ft x allowable_drawdown_ft. The inverse of specific_capacity = discharge / drawdown.
well-max-yield.edition: AWWA A100 (Water Wells) standard; USGS well-testing methods (USGS Open-File Report 02-197).
well-max-yield.freeAccess: awwa.org for the A100 TOC; pubs.usgs.gov for the USGS report.
well-max-yield.governance: Estimate. Operator of record and primacy agency govern.
well-max-yield.editionNote: The sustainable pumping rate a well can give up without pulling the water below the pump, the inverse of well-drawdown: max_yield = specific_capacity x allowable_drawdown. The specific capacity (GPM per foot of drawdown) comes from a step-drawdown test or the well-drawdown tile; the allowable drawdown is the head from the static level down to a safe level above the pump intake or the top of the screen (leave a margin so the pump never breaks suction). Specific capacity DECLINES at higher rates from well losses, so this linear estimate holds near the tested rate and overstates the yield well above it - confirm with a constant-rate test. A specific capacity below 0.5 GPM/ft is a marginal well and is flagged. A planning estimate; a pumping test and a licensed well driller govern.

assumptions.name: Linear near the test rate
assumptions.value: specific capacity declines with rate (well losses); the linear yield holds near the tested rate, overstates it far above

assumptions.name: Specific-capacity floor
assumptions.value: < 0.5 GPM/ft flagged as a marginal well

asphalt-paving-speed.formula: tons_per_hour = speed x working_min x width x (depth/12) x density / 2000; lane_ft_per_hour = speed x working_min; daily = hourly x hours.
asphalt-paving-speed.edition: Paving production identity by name (production = laydown area rate x compacted density); NAPA laydown-rate practice.
asphalt-paving-speed.freeAccess: The paving production identity is published earthmoving / paving practice; NAPA guides free at asphaltpavement.org.
asphalt-paving-speed.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
asphalt-paving-speed.editionNote: The compacted HMA density (typically ~145 pcf for a dense-graded mix) and the laydown temperature govern the real tonnage. The 50-minute hour is a planning default, not a guarantee. Match the forward speed to the plant delivery rate divided by the tons per lane-foot to keep the paver moving.

assumptions.name: Default HMA density
assumptions.value: 145 pcf unless the user supplies a mix-specific value

assumptions.name: Working minutes
assumptions.value: 50-minute hour (efficiency factor for real-world delays)

demo-debris.formula: Tonnage = volume × density (pcf) / 2000. Densities by structure type (wood-frame ~ 18 pcf, masonry ~ 110, mixed-use ~ 60). Dumpster sizing across 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 yd³ steps.
demo-debris.edition: EPA Construction and Demolition Debris Management guidance (EPA-530-K-16-002) by name; engineering-practice density values.
demo-debris.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

assumptions.name: Density per structure class
assumptions.value: engineering-practice consensus

displacement-cr.formula: Displacement (in³) = π × (bore/2)² × stroke × n_cyl. Static compression ratio CR = (V_swept_per_cyl + V_TDC) / V_TDC where V_TDC = chamber + gasket + deck − dome.
displacement-cr.edition: Classical engine-design geometry; SAE J604 displacement / SAE J1349 power-rating by name.
displacement-cr.freeAccess: SAE standards licensed; principles free in published engine-design texts.
displacement-cr.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

assumptions.name: Bore / stroke / chamber inputs
assumptions.value: user-supplied

flood-cut-quantity.formula: drywall_ft2 = wall_run_lf * (cut_height_in/12) * faces (faces = 2 if both sides); sheets_4x8 = ceil(drywall_ft2 / 32); baseboard_lf = wall_run_lf; insulation_ft2 = insulated ? wall_run_lf * (cut_height_in/12) : 0. 4x8 sheet = 32 ft2.
flood-cut-quantity.edition: IICRC S500-2021 structural-removal principle by name; standard geometry.
flood-cut-quantity.freeAccess: IICRC S500-2021 licensed; the take-off geometry is public.
flood-cut-quantity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
flood-cut-quantity.editionNote: The cut height is a field decision driven by the highest moisture reading (the wick line), not a fixed 2 ft rule. Category 3 may require removing all wet porous material; pre-1980 structures require lead / asbestos assessment first.

assumptions.name: Cut height default
assumptions.value: 24 in above the floor (editable)

assumptions.name: Sheet size
assumptions.value: 4x8 drywall = 32 ft2

ppe.formula: (reference page; no compute) PPE selection per IICRC S500-2021 / S520-2024 category mapping: Cat 1 (sanitary) - basic (gloves, boots); Cat 2 (significantly contaminated) - half-mask N95, eye, gloves, boots; Cat 3 (grossly contaminated) - full-face respirator (P100), Tyvek, gloves, boots. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134 governs respiratory-protection program where required.
ppe.edition: IICRC S500-2021 / S520-2024 by name; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134 by section.
ppe.freeAccess: 29 CFR 1910.134 free at ecfr.gov. IICRC standards licensed.
ppe.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
ppe.editionNote: Single-edition (IICRC + OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134; OSHA's RPP is required for respirator use beyond voluntary N95).

lavatory-tub-clearance.formula: lavatory: the front of the higher of the rim or the counter surface is 34 in maximum above the finish floor; hand-operated metering faucets remain open 10 seconds minimum. Bathtub: clearance in front extends the length of the tub and is 30 in wide minimum, extending 12 in beyond the wall at the head end where a permanent seat is provided - so the required clearance length = tub length + 12 in with a seat, and the tub length without.
lavatory-tub-clearance.edition: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, 606.3, 606.4, 606.5, 607.2, and 607.3. A US federal standard in the public domain, quoted directly.
lavatory-tub-clearance.freeAccess: The 2010 ADA Standards are published in full at no cost at ada.gov and by the US Access Board.
lavatory-tub-clearance.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
lavatory-tub-clearance.editionNote: Two fixtures whose rules are short enough to be skipped and specific enough to fail a remodel that measured fine everywhere else. The lavatory limit is 34 in to the front of the HIGHER of the rim or the counter surface - not the bowl, not the faucet, the higher of the two. That is why a vessel sink on a 34 in counter fails on its own rim, out by the height of the vessel, and why a thick stone top on a standard-height cabinet can be out by an inch before anything is set on it: the rim alone would have passed and the counter around it does not, so the fixture was never the problem. The tile flags that case specifically, because it changes who has to fix it. Metering faucets carry their own number that gets missed because it is not a dimension: a hand-operated metering faucet must remain open 10 SECONDS minimum, which is longer than most are shipped set and is adjusted at the cartridge rather than specified at purchase. The bathtub clearance is where the drawing goes short. It runs THE LENGTH OF THE TUB and is 30 in wide minimum - and where a permanent seat is provided at the head end it extends 12 in BEYOND the wall at that end, so a 60 in tub with a permanent seat needs 72 in of clear floor. The fixture is one length and the floor it needs is another, and the 12 in past a wall is the part nobody draws. Not checked: the clear floor space at the lavatory and the knee and toe clearance under it, which are separate tiles (knee-toe-clearance checks the knee and toe space) and which a cabinet defeats before the height does; whether faucet controls meet the operable-parts requirements for force and one-hand operation; the 606.5 requirement that supply and drain pipes under a lavatory be insulated or otherwise configured to protect against contact with no sharp or abrasive surfaces beneath, which is quoted here but is not a measurable this tile checks; grab bars at the tub, which have their own geometry and their own tile; the tub seat itself, permanent or removable, and its dimensions; controls, faucets, and the hand shower; enclosures, which may not obstruct transfer; and state and local accessibility law and the plumbing code. A clearance screen, not a bathroom design.

assumptions.name: Lavatory height
assumptions.value: 34 in maximum to the front of the HIGHER of the rim or counter surface

assumptions.name: Metering faucets
assumptions.value: remain open 10 seconds minimum

assumptions.name: Pipe protection
assumptions.value: insulated or otherwise configured to protect against contact; quoted, not measured here

assumptions.name: Tub clearance
assumptions.value: the length of the bathtub, 30 in wide minimum

assumptions.name: Permanent seat
assumptions.value: clearance extends 12 in beyond the wall at the head end

assumptions.name: Seat required
assumptions.value: a permanent seat at the head end or a removable in-tub seat

nernst-equation.formula: E = E0 - (RT/nF) ln Q; R = 8.314 J/(mol*K), F = 96485 C/mol, T in kelvin. At 25 C the slope is 0.05916/n V per decade of Q. Nernst slope = RT ln(10)/(nF).
nernst-equation.edition: The Nernst equation (Nernst, 1889); standard electrochemistry. First principles.
nernst-equation.freeAccess: The Nernst equation and the constants R and F are public first-principles chemistry; the standard potential, electron count, and reaction quotient are the user's own inputs.
nernst-equation.governance: Verify protocol against your lab's SOP before pipetting. A miscalculated dilution can ruin a run or a sample.
nernst-equation.editionNote: The cell or electrode potential away from standard conditions. The Nernst equation corrects the standard potential E0 for the actual mix of reactants and products: E = E0 - (RT/nF) ln Q, where n is the electrons transferred, F = 96485 C/mol is the Faraday constant, and Q is the reaction quotient (the ratio of product to reactant activities, approximated by concentrations). At 25 C the group RT/F ln(10) is 0.05916 V, so each tenfold change in Q shifts the potential by 0.05916/n V; a one-electron pH electrode gives the familiar 59 mV per pH unit. When Q = 1 the potential equals E0. This uses concentrations for activities and ignores liquid-junction potential and kinetic overpotential; for accurate work at high ionic strength use activities. A first-principles chemistry aid; the measured electrochemistry governs.

assumptions.name: Nernst equation
assumptions.value: E = E0 - (RT/nF) ln Q; R = 8.314, F = 96485, T in kelvin

assumptions.name: 25 C slope
assumptions.value: 0.05916/n V per decade of Q (59 mV/pH for n = 1)

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: activities approximated by concentrations; excludes junction potential and overpotential

amortization-schedule.formula: Monthly P&I = (P * r) / (1 - (1 + r)^-n) where r = APR/12 and n = term in months. Per-row: interest = balance * r; principal = payment - interest + extra; balance = balance - principal; loop until balance <= 0 or n reached.
amortization-schedule.edition: Standard mortgage amortization (closed-form annuity formula). FNMA Single-Family Selling Guide §B2-1.2 (loan term and amortization). 12 CFR §1026.18 (truth-in-lending payment schedule disclosure).
amortization-schedule.freeAccess: FNMA Selling Guide free at selling-guide.fanniemae.com. 12 CFR Part 1026 (Regulation Z) free at ecfr.gov.
amortization-schedule.governance: Estimate. Lender governs final underwriting and rate / fee disclosure. Appraiser governs the appraised value. State law and the agency's program guidelines may impose stricter limits than the published thresholds.
amortization-schedule.editionNote: Extra-principal posting rules vary by lender and product. Some servicers apply extra principal immediately (preferred); some hold it for the next due date; some require explicit borrower instruction. Lender governs.

assumptions.name: Extra principal posting
assumptions.value: applied immediately each month before next interest accrual

assumptions.name: Rounding
assumptions.value: no per-payment rounding; balance closes within $0.01 floating-point precision

max-grid-resistance-for-touch.formula: max_grid_resistance_ohm = tolerable_touch_v / grid_current_a, the IEEE 80 GPR screen GPR = grid_current x grid_resistance solved for the resistance that keeps GPR at or below the tolerable touch voltage.
max-grid-resistance-for-touch.edition: IEEE Std 80 ground potential rise, solved for the grid resistance, by name.
max-grid-resistance-for-touch.freeAccess: IEEE 80 is available through IEEE; the ground-potential-rise relation is a published grounding-study screen.
max-grid-resistance-for-touch.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
max-grid-resistance-for-touch.editionNote: The inverse of ground-potential-rise: the grid resistance target that keeps the whole yard's ground potential rise at or below the tolerable touch voltage, so the IEEE 80 screen passes without a mesh/step study. A lower grid resistance (more rods, a larger mesh, or better soil) or a lower grid current is needed if the target is impractical. The grid current is the portion of fault current returning through the grid to remote earth, not the total fault. IEEE Std 80 and a qualified grounding study govern - a screen, not a grounding design.

assumptions.name: Resistance target
assumptions.value: max_R_g = tolerable_touch / grid_current clears the yard without mesh/step analysis

assumptions.name: Grid current
assumptions.value: I_G is the portion of fault current returning through the grid to remote earth, not the total fault

neutral-grounding-resistor.formula: V_LN = V_LL / sqrt(3); R = V_LN / I_ground; P = I_ground^2 x R (= V_LN x I_ground).
neutral-grounding-resistor.edition: Neutral grounding resistor sizing (IEEE 142 grounding practice), first-principles, by name; IEEE 142 and the protection scheme govern.
neutral-grounding-resistor.freeAccess: The NGR sizing relation is first-principles Ohm's law on the line-to-neutral voltage; the system voltage and target fault current come from the design.
neutral-grounding-resistor.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
neutral-grounding-resistor.editionNote: Neutral grounding resistor sizing. The resistor sees the LINE-TO-NEUTRAL voltage, V_LN = V_LL / sqrt(3), not the line-to-line -- sizing off V_LL makes the resistor sqrt(3) too large and the fault current too small to detect. R = V_LN / I_ground and P = I_ground^2 x R (which equals V_LN x I_ground). A high-resistance ground (HRG) limits the fault to a few amps and lets the plant run through the first fault; its resistor is rated for continuous dissipation. A low-resistance ground (LRG) limits it to 100 to 400 A for fast coordinated tripping; its resistor is rated only for the short trip time. For an HRG the resistor current must exceed the system's total charging current to control transient overvoltage. A design aid, not the engineer of record; IEEE 142 and the protection scheme govern.

assumptions.name: Line-to-neutral
assumptions.value: the resistor sees V_LL / sqrt(3); sizing off V_LL makes it sqrt(3) too large

assumptions.name: HRG vs LRG
assumptions.value: HRG limits to a few amps (continuous rating); LRG to 100-400 A (short-time rating)

assumptions.name: Charging current
assumptions.value: the HRG resistor current must exceed the system charging current to control overvoltage

capacitor-bank-for-resonance-order.formula: MVAR_cap = MVA_sc / h_target^2, the parallel-resonance relation h = sqrt(MVA_sc / MVAR_cap) solved for the bank (the maximum bank that keeps the resonant order at or above the target).
capacitor-bank-for-resonance-order.edition: Parallel-resonance order of a power-factor capacitor bank (IEEE 519 / IEEE 1531) solved for the bank, first-principles, by name; a harmonic study governs.
capacitor-bank-for-resonance-order.freeAccess: The h = sqrt(MVA_sc / MVAR_cap) resonance relation is a published first-principles result; the bus short-circuit level comes from the system data.
capacitor-bank-for-resonance-order.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
capacitor-bank-for-resonance-order.editionNote: The inverse of harmonic-resonance: the largest power-factor capacitor bank that keeps the parallel-resonance order at or above a target. Because a bigger bank lowers the resonant order toward the strong low-order harmonics, a target just below the lowest harmonic of concern (about 4.7 to stay under the 5th) sets a ceiling on the bank; split the correction into smaller banks, add a detuning reactor (making it a filter), or run a harmonic study if power factor needs more. The estimate uses the bus short-circuit level and ignores load and resistive damping. A screening aid, not a harmonic study.

assumptions.name: Bank ceiling
assumptions.value: MVAR_cap = MVA_sc / h_target^2 keeps the resonant order at or above the target

assumptions.name: Bigger bank, lower order
assumptions.value: a larger capacitor bank lowers the resonant order toward the strong low harmonics

assumptions.name: Idealized
assumptions.value: ignores load and resistive damping; a detuning reactor or harmonic study is the fix

transformer-k-factor.formula: K = sum(Ih^2 x h^2) / sum(Ih^2) over h = 1,3,5,7,9,11,13 with harmonics in per-unit of the fundamental; round up to the next standard K-rating (K-1, K-4, K-9, K-13, K-20, K-30, K-40).
transformer-k-factor.edition: Transformer K-factor for nonlinear loads, UL 1561 and IEEE C57.110, by name.
transformer-k-factor.freeAccess: The K-factor weights each harmonic by the square of its order; a near-linear load (K close to 1) needs only the lowest K rating, K-4; only a pure sine (K exactly 1) stays at K-1. The measured spectrum and the manufacturer govern the final selection.
transformer-k-factor.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
transformer-k-factor.editionNote: Single-edition (UL 1561 / IEEE C57.110 K-factor convention; refresh as the standards revise).

assumptions.name: K-factor definition
assumptions.value: sum of (per-unit harmonic current squared times harmonic order squared) divided by the sum of (per-unit harmonic current squared)

assumptions.name: Standard K-ratings
assumptions.value: the tabulated ladder K-1 (standard) / K-4 / K-9 / K-13 / K-20 / K-30 / K-40

chain-link-fence-takeoff.formula: fabric_lf = rail_wire_lf = perimeter_ft - gate_width_ft; total_posts = ceil(perimeter_ft / line_post_spacing_ft); terminals = corners + (gate jambs); line_posts = total_posts - terminals; tension_bands = (2 x corners + gate jambs) x ceil(height_ft - 1).
chain-link-fence-takeoff.edition: Chain-link takeoff identity by name (fabric net of gates; posts over the run; bands per terminal per foot of height); first-principles count arithmetic.
chain-link-fence-takeoff.freeAccess: The count arithmetic is public first-principles; the fabric gauge, post schedule, and hardware follow the fence spec.
chain-link-fence-takeoff.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
chain-link-fence-takeoff.editionNote: Line posts run about 10 ft on center. Terminals (corners, ends, gate jambs) each get tension bands, a rail end, and a brace; corners take two sets of bands (Master Halco, Hoover). The fabric is stretched against a tension wire and bar. Gate hardware is taken off separately. Distinct from the generic fence-estimate.

assumptions.name: Line post spacing
assumptions.value: ~10 ft on center (default); the fence spec governs

assumptions.name: Tension bands
assumptions.value: one per foot of height less one (rounded up) per set; two sets at a corner, one at an end or gate jamb

sill-plate-anchor-count.formula: effective_len_ft = wall_length_ft - 2 x (end_distance_in/12); bolts = max(2, ceil(effective_len_ft / max_spacing_ft) + 1).
sill-plate-anchor-count.edition: Sill-plate anchor-count rule by name (bolts from the span between end bolts over the max spacing, min two); IRC R403.1.6.
sill-plate-anchor-count.freeAccess: The anchor-count layout is public IRC R403.1.6 prescriptive geometry; the adopted code edition and any engineered plan govern.
sill-plate-anchor-count.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
sill-plate-anchor-count.editionNote: IRC R403.1.6 caps the spacing at 6 ft (high-wind and seismic provisions or engineered plans tighten it). Each plate section gets a minimum of two bolts, one within 12 in of each end and corner. A 1/2 in bolt needs at least 7 in of embedment. The adopted code and any engineered plan govern; distinct from the anchor-embedment capacity calc.

assumptions.name: Max spacing
assumptions.value: 6 ft per IRC R403.1.6; high-wind/seismic or engineered plans tighten it

assumptions.name: End distance
assumptions.value: a bolt within 12 in of each end and corner; minimum two bolts per plate

frustum-volume.formula: V = (pi h/12)(D^2 + D d + d^2); L = sqrt(h^2 + (R-r)^2), R=D/2, r=d/2; lateral area = pi(R+r)L. d=0 -> full cone, d=D -> cylinder.
frustum-volume.edition: The conical frustum volume V = (pi h/12)(D^2 + D d + d^2) and lateral surface pi(R+r)L - standard solid geometry as in Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press), by name; public domain.
frustum-volume.freeAccess: Pure solid geometry, public; the two diameters and the height are user-supplied measurements.
frustum-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
frustum-volume.editionNote: Volume, slant height, and lateral (side-only) surface of a right conical frustum - a truncated cone, the shape of a hopper, a bucket, a tapered footing or pier, a flat-topped stockpile, or a round-to-round transition. The volume is V = (pi h/12)(D^2 + D d + d^2) with the large and small diameters D and d and the height h; setting d = 0 gives a full cone (V = pi D^2 h/12) and d = D a cylinder. It is reported in cubic feet, US gallons, and cubic yards so it serves a liquid fill, a concrete pour, or a material takeoff. Note it is more than the average-diameter guess: the frustum formula, not the mean diameter, is the right one. The slant height is L = sqrt(h^2 + (R-r)^2) and the lateral area is pi(R+r)L (the sloped wall, no ends). The end-disk areas, wall thickness, an eccentric (offset) cone, and a pyramidal (flat-sided) hopper are separate. A takeoff aid; verify against the drawing.

assumptions.name: Frustum volume
assumptions.value: V = (pi h/12)(D^2 + D d + d^2); more than the mean-diameter guess

assumptions.name: Slant / lateral
assumptions.value: L = sqrt(h^2 + (R-r)^2); lateral area = pi(R+r)L (no ends)

assumptions.name: Limits
assumptions.value: d=0 gives a full cone, d=D a cylinder; offset/pyramidal shapes are separate

spherical-cap-volume.formula: R = D/2; V_cap = (pi h^2/3)(3R - h); V_full = (4/3) pi R^3; percent full = V_cap/V_full. h=R hemisphere, h=D full sphere.
spherical-cap-volume.edition: The spherical-cap volume V = (pi h^2/3)(3R - h) and the full-sphere volume (4/3) pi R^3 - standard solid geometry as in Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press), by name; public domain.
spherical-cap-volume.freeAccess: Pure solid geometry, public; the sphere diameter and fill depth are user-supplied measurements.
spherical-cap-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
spherical-cap-volume.editionNote: Volume of a spherical cap - the partial fill of a spherical tank, the volume of a dome or a dished tank bottom, or a hemispherical vessel: V = (pi h^2/3)(3R - h) for a fill depth h measured from the bottom of the sphere up to the liquid line (or the height of a dome), with R = D/2. The full sphere is (4/3) pi R^3. At h = R the cap is a hemisphere (exactly half the sphere); at h = D it is the full sphere. A sphere is narrow near the bottom, so a shallow fill holds far less than a straight-sided estimate - 3 ft in a 10 ft sphere is 21.6% full, not 30% - which is why a spherical or dished-bottom tank needs this formula. Reported in cubic feet and US gallons for a dipstick or a takeoff. A spherical zone between two levels, an ellipsoidal (2:1) tank head, and the surface area are separate. A takeoff / dipstick aid; verify against the tank chart or drawing.

assumptions.name: Cap volume
assumptions.value: V = (pi h^2/3)(3R - h); h from the bottom of the sphere

assumptions.name: Limits
assumptions.value: h = R is a hemisphere (half), h = D the full sphere (4/3 pi R^3)

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: cap only; spherical zone, ellipsoidal head, and surface area are separate

cone-bottom-tank-volume.formula: R = D/2; volume = (pi R^2/(3 Hc^2)) h^3 for h <= Hc, else (1/3) pi R^2 Hc + pi R^2 (h - Hc); full = (1/3) pi R^2 Hc + pi R^2 Hcyl.
cone-bottom-tank-volume.edition: Cone-bottom vertical tank partial gauging - a right cone from the apex plus a straight cylinder; standard solid geometry (cone + cylinder) as in Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press), by name; public domain.
cone-bottom-tank-volume.freeAccess: Public-domain solid geometry; the diameter, cone height, cylinder height, and depth are user-supplied.
cone-bottom-tank-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
cone-bottom-tank-volume.editionNote: Partial volume of a vertical cone-bottom (conical / hopper bottom) tank from a dipstick depth measured up from the bottom apex - the poly, process, or feed tank the flat-bottom tank-volume tile does not cover. Below the cone height Hc the liquid fills a cone whose radius grows with height, r(h) = R h/Hc, so the volume is (pi R^2/(3 Hc^2)) h^3; above Hc it is the full cone (1/3) pi R^2 Hc plus a straight cylinder pi R^2 (h - Hc). Because the cone empties as the cube of the depth, a dipstick low in the cone reads far less than a straight-side guess. Enter the inside diameter, the cone (bottom) height, the straight-side (cylinder) height, and the depth from the apex, all in feet. A right cone concentric with the cylinder, apex down; a flat-bottom tank is the tank-volume tile, and the tank's own chart governs. Reported in cubic feet and US gallons with the percent full.

assumptions.name: Cone region
assumptions.value: V = (pi R^2/(3 Hc^2)) h^3, a right cone from the apex with r(h) = R h/Hc

assumptions.name: Cylinder region
assumptions.value: full cone + pi R^2 (h - Hc) above the cone height

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: right cone concentric with the cylinder, apex down; a flat-bottom tank is the tank-volume tile

gear-dynamic-tooth-stress.formula: D = T / Pd; torque = 63,025 HP / rpm (in-lb); Wt = 2 x torque / D; V = pi D N / 12 (ft/min); Kv = (1200 + V)/1200 for cut or milled teeth, (600 + V)/600 for cast or crude; static sigma = Wt Pd / (F Y) delegated to the landed Lewis tile; dynamic sigma = static x Kv x 1.42 when the gear is an idler; allowable = Sut/3 when a material strength is entered.
gear-dynamic-tooth-stress.edition: Barth velocity factor applied to the Lewis (1892, public domain) bending equation, as taught in the standard machine-design treatment. The worked example this tile reproduces exactly - a 43-tooth, 20 degree full involute, 8 diametral pitch, 0.5 in wide pinion transmitting 4 HP at 1,000 rpm, giving 8,152 psi - is from W. H. Dornfeld, ME312 Tooth Strength notes (Fairfield University, 2006), following Hamrock Eqs. 14.55 and following.
gear-dynamic-tooth-stress.freeAccess: Lewis is public domain and the Barth factor is published in free university course notes and machine-design references. No AGMA table, quality-number chart, or geometry-factor curve is reproduced here - none is used.
gear-dynamic-tooth-stress.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
gear-dynamic-tooth-stress.editionNote: The reason this tile exists is that the static Lewis number is badly optimistic on a real drive. In the pinned example the pitch line runs 1,407 ft/min, Kv comes out 2.17, and the bending stress MORE THAN DOUBLES from 3,752 to 8,152 psi - the same tooth, the same load, just moving. Cast or crude teeth take the harsher 600 base rather than 1200 because a rough profile hammers harder at every mesh. An idler carries an additional 1.42 because it is driven on one flank and drives on the other, so its teeth see a fully reversed cycle rather than a released one. Starting from horsepower and rpm rather than from a tangential load removes the step where most arithmetic errors happen. The static stress is delegated to the landed gear-tooth-bending-stress tile rather than reimplemented, and the fuzzer pins that the two agree exactly, so a fix to the Lewis form factor propagates automatically. Honest limits: Barth is an approximation and a conservative one - it is the ancestor of the AGMA dynamic factor Kv, which is tailored to a measured gear quality number and typically lands between 1 and 1.8, so this will read high against a good-quality gear. Sut/3 is the rough allowable used when no material value is on hand, not a rated endurance limit. Not modeled: the AGMA application, size, load-distribution, and rim-thickness factors, the geometry factor J that corrects Y for stress concentration, and any surface-durability (pitting) check - which frequently governs before bending does. A screen; AGMA 2001 and the gear maker govern.

assumptions.name: Barth velocity factor
assumptions.value: (1200 + V)/1200 cut or milled; (600 + V)/600 cast or crude; V in ft/min
assumptions.source: Barth, as published in standard machine-design references

assumptions.name: Load from power
assumptions.value: torque = 63,025 HP / rpm; Wt = 2 torque / D; V = pi D N / 12

assumptions.name: Static stress
assumptions.value: delegated to computeGearToothBendingStress, not reimplemented

assumptions.name: Idler factor
assumptions.value: 1.42 for fully reversed bending

assumptions.name: Allowable
assumptions.value: Sut/3, a rough estimate when no material allowable is available

assumptions.name: Not modeled
assumptions.value: AGMA Ka, Ks, Km, KB, the geometry factor J, and surface durability (pitting)

menu-engineering.formula: contribution_margin = price - food_cost; popularity_share = units_sold / total_units; popularity_threshold = (1 / item_count) x 0.70; quadrant from margin >= average and share >= threshold.
menu-engineering.edition: Kasavana & Smith menu-engineering model, by name.
menu-engineering.freeAccess: Standard hospitality menu-analysis model; the operator's cost and pricing data govern.
menu-engineering.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
menu-engineering.editionNote: The margin axis is contribution-margin dollars, not food-cost percent (a low-food-cost item can still be a Dog if it earns few dollars); popularity is judged against the menu-average share times the 0.70 rule; the classification needs the full sales mix, not a single dish. An analysis aid, not a pricing decision.

assumptions.name: Popularity rule
assumptions.value: 70% of the menu-average share (1/item_count x 0.70) is the high/low popularity cutoff

hazmat-placard-threshold.formula: table2_aggregate_lb = sum of the GROSS weight of every Table 2 material aboard, across all hazard classes; placard required when that aggregate is at least 1,001 lb, when any Table 1 material is aboard in any quantity, or when any material is in a bulk packaging (the 1,001 lb exception excludes bulk packagings).
hazmat-placard-threshold.edition: 49 CFR 172.504 placarding thresholds -- Table 1 materials placarded at any quantity, Table 2 materials at a 1,001 lb aggregate gross weight across all Table 2 classes on the vehicle -- cited by section and not reproduced. 49 CFR 172 in full, the shipper's papers, and the carrier's hazmat program govern.
hazmat-placard-threshold.freeAccess: The thresholds are public federal law, cited by section rather than mirrored, and the aggregation is addition on the shipment's own gross weights.
hazmat-placard-threshold.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
hazmat-placard-threshold.editionNote: The placarding rule splits hazardous materials into two tables. Table 1 materials, among them explosives of divisions 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3, poison-inhalation-hazard materials and certain radioactives, must be placarded at any quantity with no threshold whatever. Table 2 covers everything else, and a vehicle carrying Table 2 materials must be placarded once the aggregate gross weight of all of them reaches one thousand and one pounds. Two details cause most of the errors in practice. The first is that the aggregate runs across all Table 2 hazard classes on the vehicle rather than per class, so six hundred pounds of flammable liquid alongside five hundred pounds of corrosive is eleven hundred pounds aggregate and the vehicle gets placarded for both. The second is that it is gross weight, package and contents together, not net product weight, and drums and totes weigh a great deal empty. The most consequential misunderstanding is what falling under the threshold actually buys. Shipping papers, package marking and labeling, segregation, emergency response information and driver training have no thousand-pound threshold and apply at any quantity. Under 1,001 pounds is a placarding exemption, not a hazmat exemption, and treating it as one is how carriers end up cited.

assumptions.name: Table 1
assumptions.value: placarded at ANY quantity, no threshold

assumptions.name: Table 2 aggregate
assumptions.value: 1,001 lb aggregate GROSS weight across ALL Table 2 classes on the vehicle, not per class

assumptions.name: Bulk packagings
assumptions.value: the 1,001 lb exception opens 'Except for bulk packagings'; a liquid container over 119 gal (a 275 or 330 gal tote) is bulk, so it is placarded at any weight

assumptions.name: Placarding only
assumptions.value: papers, marking, labeling, segregation, emergency response information, and training have no threshold

scaffold-platform-check.formula: worst gap = max(gap between adjacent units, gap between platform and uprights), capped at 1 in; platform width >= 18 in; maximum overhang = 12 in where the platform length is 10 ft or less and 18 in where it is greater, satisfied either within the limit or by a designed non-tipping cantilever; front edge <= 14 in from the face of the work, satisfied either within the limit or by front-edge guardrails and/or personal fall arrest.
scaffold-platform-check.edition: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.451(b), Subpart L - Scaffolds. A US federal regulation in the public domain, quoted directly.
scaffold-platform-check.freeAccess: 29 CFR is published in full at no cost by OSHA and the eCFR.
scaffold-platform-check.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
scaffold-platform-check.editionNote: The finding is that the overhang limit follows the BOARD rather than the bay. A platform 10 ft or less may not extend over its support more than 12 in; one greater than 10 ft may not extend more than 18. So an identical 15 in overhang fails on an 8 ft plank and passes on a 16 ft one, and swapping a single long plank for two short ones tightens the allowable overhang from 18 in to 12 with nothing else on the scaffold changing. Both limits carry the same escape - unless the platform is designed and installed so that the cantilevered portion can support employees and materials without tipping - which makes a long overhang a design question rather than a flat prohibition, and the tile treats it that way rather than reporting a violation. The gap rule is worth reading twice because it runs two ways: no more than 1 in between adjacent units AND no more than 1 in between the platform and the uprights. The second is the one that gets forgotten, because it is a gap against the frame rather than between two boards, and it is exactly where a foot goes. The 14 in front-edge limit has its own escape in guardrails along the front edge and/or personal fall arrest, so it is a choice between closing the gap and protecting the edge rather than a hard dimension; outrigger scaffolds and plastering and lathing operations carry their own front-edge figures, which this tile does not apply. One requirement is deliberately NOT computed: the MINIMUM distance a plank must extend over the centerline of its support unless cleated or restrained. It is real, it sits in the same paragraph, it works in the opposite direction from the maximums above, and it is what keeps a plank from being levered off its bearer - but it could not be confirmed from a primary source, so no figure is asserted and the note says to read the paragraph for it. Also not checked: whether the platform is fully planked or decked between the front upright and the guardrail; unit overlap and end conditions; plank grade, span, and rated load, which is a strength calculation rather than a dimension; ties, bracing, and foundations; and the guardrail system, which has its own tile. A screen, not a scaffold plan; Subpart L and the competent person govern.

assumptions.name: Gaps
assumptions.value: 1 in maximum between adjacent units AND between the platform and the uprights

assumptions.name: Width
assumptions.value: at least 18 in for each platform and walkway

assumptions.name: Front edge
assumptions.value: not more than 14 in from the face of the work, unless guardrails and/or PFAS

assumptions.name: Overhang
assumptions.value: 12 in at 10 ft or less, 18 in over 10 ft - the limit follows the plank length

assumptions.name: Cantilever escape
assumptions.value: either limit is met by a design that supports the cantilever without tipping

assumptions.name: Minimum bearing
assumptions.value: the minimum extension over the support is real but unverified here and is NOT asserted

footing-eccentric-pressure.formula: e = M/P; e <= B/6: q = (P/BL)(1 +/- 6e/B); e > B/6: q_max = 2P/(3L(B/2 - e)), q_min = 0, bearing length = 3(B/2 - e).
footing-eccentric-pressure.edition: The eccentric spread-footing bearing-pressure relations - the middle-third (kern) trapezoidal form and the resultant-outside-kern triangular form - a standard foundation-engineering result, by name.
footing-eccentric-pressure.freeAccess: The eccentric-footing pressure relations and the middle-third rule are public foundation-engineering results.
footing-eccentric-pressure.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
footing-eccentric-pressure.editionNote: The middle-third rule q = (P/BL)(1 +/- 6e/B) for e <= B/6 and the resultant-outside-kern q_max = 2P/(3L(B/2 - e)), q_min = 0 for e > B/6, with e = M/P. This returns the service bearing pressure distribution under a one-way eccentric or axial-plus-moment load - it covers uniaxial eccentricity (a biaxial ex, ey load needs the two-way form), assumes a rigid footing on a linear-elastic soil (no soil-model refinement), and does not check the allowable bearing, settlement, or the footing's own flexure/shear. A design aid, not a substitute for the structural/geotechnical engineer of record's design.

assumptions.name: Kern rule
assumptions.value: trapezoidal q = (P/BL)(1 +/- 6e/B) while e <= B/6 (full bearing)

assumptions.name: Outside kern
assumptions.value: heel lifts to a triangle over 3(B/2 - e) with q_max = 2P/(3L(B/2 - e))

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: uniaxial eccentricity, rigid footing; allowable bearing and settlement are separate

masonry-anchor-bolt.formula: Apt = pi x lbe^2; Bab = 1.25 x Apt x sqrt(f'm) (masonry breakout, ASD); Bas = 0.6 x Ab x fy (steel); Ba = min(Bab, Bas).
masonry-anchor-bolt.edition: TMS 402 (Building Code Requirements for Masonry Structures) allowable-stress anchor-bolt tension provisions, as compiled in the Masonry Designers' Guide and CMHA TEK notes, by name.
masonry-anchor-bolt.freeAccess: CMHA TEK notes on anchor-bolt design are free public CMHA technical notes; the 1.25 x Apt x sqrt(f'm) and 0.6 x Ab x fy arithmetic is public.
masonry-anchor-bolt.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
masonry-anchor-bolt.editionNote: TMS 402 allowable-stress design of a headed anchor bolt in axial tension in grouted masonry: the allowable tension is the LESSER of the masonry breakout Bab = 1.25 x Apt x sqrt(f'm), with Apt = pi x lbe^2 the projected area of the 45-degree tension breakout cone (lbe the effective embedment), and the steel Bas = 0.6 x Ab x fy (Ab the bolt tensile-stress area, fy its yield). A shallow anchor pulls a cone of masonry out (masonry governs); a deep enough anchor makes the steel yield first (steel governs). The full-cone Apt is an upper bound - edge distance, or overlapping cones from closely spaced anchors, reduce it (a separate reduction the designer applies); anchor shear and combined shear-tension (pryout) are separate checks. The corresponding strength-design coefficient is 4 x Apt x sqrt(f'm). fy defaults to 36,000 psi (ASTM A307 / F1554 Grade 36). A design aid, not a substitute for the engineer of record's stamped design.

assumptions.name: Lesser of two modes
assumptions.value: the allowable is the lesser of masonry breakout Bab = 1.25 x Apt x sqrt(f'm) and steel Bas = 0.6 x Ab x fy

assumptions.name: Full-cone projected area
assumptions.value: Apt = pi x lbe^2 assumes a full breakout cone; edge distance or overlapping cones reduce Apt

assumptions.name: Tension only
assumptions.value: axial tension only; anchor shear (pryout) and combined shear-tension are separate checks

transverse-wind-load-conductor.formula: wind pressure p = 0.00256 V^2 where a speed is entered; force on a conductor = p x (diameter / 12) x wind span x conductor count; force on a pole = p x its tapered projected area with the resultant at the trapezoid centroid, h/3 x (B + 2T)/(B + T) above the groundline (B groundline, T top diameter); groundline moment = the sum of each force times its height.
transverse-wind-load-conductor.edition: The transverse wind load relations by name, with the ASCE 7 velocity-pressure constant 0.00256 -- the same relation the wind-pressure calculator uses. Round shape factor 1.0; NO gust response, height adjustment, or terrain exposure factor is applied, so this is a screen rather than a design. The applicable NESC edition, the utility's construction standards, and a qualified line designer govern.
transverse-wind-load-conductor.freeAccess: Pressure times projected area on dimensions the user supplies; no wind map or exposure table is reproduced.
transverse-wind-load-conductor.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
transverse-wind-load-conductor.editionNote: The load that governs a distribution structure on a windy day is not the conductor tension, it is the wind on the conductors and on the pole, and both land at different heights and become a moment. The projected area of a cylinder is diameter times length, so a conductor's wind load per foot is its diameter in inches over twelve times the pressure and nothing else. THE LENGTH THAT COUNTS IS THE WIND SPAN, half the span on each side of the structure, which is not the ruling span and not the weight span -- confusing wind span with weight span is the standard error on an angle or hillside structure. The pole carries its own wind on a tapered area with the resultant at the trapezoid centroid, a little below mid-height because the pole is wider at the bottom, and while that force is small next to the conductors its moment arm is not: a 9 psf wind on one Drake at a 400 ft wind span gives 332 lb at 38 ft against the pole's 293 lb at 18.2 ft, which is 30% of a 17,955 ft-lb total. Under ice the diameter grows and so does the wind area, which is why the district cases combine ice AND wind.

assumptions.name: Wind span, not ruling span or weight span
assumptions.value: the standard error on an angle or hillside structure

assumptions.name: No gust, height, or exposure factor
assumptions.value: a screen, not a grade-of-construction design

assumptions.name: Transverse only
assumptions.value: longitudinal deadend loads and angle tension components are not computed

spcc-containment-volume.formula: required volume = the largest single container's capacity x (1 + freeboard); gross dike volume = length x width x wall height; displacement = the volume of tanks and equipment standing inside up to that height; net capacity = gross minus displacement, at 1728/231 cubic inches per gallon.
spcc-containment-volume.edition: Secondary containment sizing as SPCC practice states it -- capacity for the LARGEST SINGLE container plus freeboard, with NET capacity being gross minus the displacement of everything inside. It treats the dike as a rectangular prism. It does not determine SPCC applicability or the required freeboard, address the alternative sized-containment provisions for loading racks, mobile containers or oil-filled equipment, evaluate imperviousness or drainage control, or substitute for the PE certification the rule requires.
spcc-containment-volume.freeAccess: One volume minus another; no rule text is reproduced.
spcc-containment-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
spcc-containment-volume.editionNote: The requirement is the LARGEST SINGLE container plus freeboard, not the sum of the tanks, because the design event is one container failing. The DISPLACEMENT subtraction is what gets missed: a dike sized to hold the largest tank looks adequate until the other tanks, their ring foundations and a pump skid are counted, and on a congested tank farm that displacement can turn a comfortable margin into a deficiency. Two conditions matter as much as the volume and neither is arithmetic -- a dike with an open drain valve has NO capacity, and containment must be sufficiently impervious to hold the oil long enough to recover it.

assumptions.name: A rectangular prism
assumptions.value: sloped walls and irregular footprints are not modelled

assumptions.name: Freeboard is entered
assumptions.value: the applicable storm event or percentage is a rule question

assumptions.name: Not a compliance determination
assumptions.value: the PE certification the rule requires is not replaced

lift-bag-sizing.formula: in-water weight = W (1 - rho_w / rho_obj); required lift = in-water weight + breakout; bag volume = required lift / rho_w (64 lb/cu ft seawater, 62.4 fresh); free air = bag volume x (D + Dw)/Dw, Dw = 2,116.2/rho_w ft per atmosphere (33.07 ft seawater, 33.9 ft fresh); bags = ceil(required lift / bag rating).
lift-bag-sizing.edition: Buoyancy (Archimedes) and Boyle's law as the U.S. Navy Salvage Manual applies them to lift bags and pontoons, by name.
lift-bag-sizing.freeAccess: The U.S. Navy Salvage Manual is published free by NAVSEA; the relations are first-principles physics on the user's weight, density, depth, and bag rating.
lift-bag-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
lift-bag-sizing.editionNote: Static lift only: the bag must displace the in-water weight plus any breakout force from bottom suction, which can equal or exceed the object's weight. Air expands as a bag rises, so a bag that just lifts at depth accelerates toward the surface; open-bottom bags, dump valves, and rigging govern control. Not a lift plan; the dive supervisor governs.

assumptions.name: Water density
assumptions.value: 64 lb/cu ft seawater, 62.4 lb/cu ft fresh

assumptions.name: Depth per atmosphere
assumptions.value: 2,116.2 lb/sq ft over the water density: 33.07 ft seawater, 33.9 ft fresh (the Navy rounds to 33 and 34)

assumptions.name: Breakout
assumptions.value: entered; bottom suction is site-specific

coating-breakdown-factor.formula: f(t) = f(0) + annual rate x t, capped at 1.0; current = area x bare-steel current density x f(t); mean at f(0) + rate x life / 2.
coating-breakdown-factor.edition: Linear coating breakdown per DNV-RP-B401 and NACE practice. The CP designer governs the factors.
coating-breakdown-factor.freeAccess: DNV-RP-B401 is freely downloadable from DNV.
coating-breakdown-factor.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
coating-breakdown-factor.editionNote: The mean current buys anode metal; the final current buys anode count and rectifier capacity. Sizing everything on commissioning current leaves a system at a small fraction of its end-of-life requirement.

assumptions.name: Degradation
assumptions.value: linear, the customary design model

assumptions.name: Ceiling
assumptions.value: the breakdown factor caps at fully bare steel

collection-route-productivity.formula: collection time = stops x seconds per stop; route tonnage = stops x average setout weight; disposal loads = tonnage / payload rounded up; route day = collection + haul + tipping + fixed and break time.
collection-route-productivity.edition: Element build-up. The operation's own time study and any applicable collective bargaining agreement govern a standard used to staff or to pay.
collection-route-productivity.freeAccess: Public method; the element times are the operation's own measurements.
collection-route-productivity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
collection-route-productivity.editionNote: The cliff is what to watch: when tonnage crosses a multiple of the payload the day gets a whole haul cycle longer overnight, which is why routes are watched in TONS rather than stops.

assumptions.name: Element times
assumptions.value: entered from the operation's own study rather than assumed

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: one route on one shift; it does not sequence the route or model traffic

rooftop-curb-uplift.formula: uplift = plan area x the zone's net uplift pressure (ASD level), resisted by 0.6 x the unit weight (ASCE 7 ASD 0.6 D + 0.6 W); lateral wind on the side profile acts at mid-height, and the moment resolves across the unit width as a couple adding tension to the windward fasteners.
rooftop-curb-uplift.edition: The design pressures are ENTERED for the roof zone and height. Rooftop equipment carries its own provisions, distinct from the roof covering's, and edge and corner zones are much worse than the field.
rooftop-curb-uplift.freeAccess: Areas, one moment, and one division.
rooftop-curb-uplift.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
rooftop-curb-uplift.editionNote: THE DIRECTION IS REPORTED IN WORDS, NOT AS A SIGNED NUMBER, because spec-v1636 read its own sign backwards. Its unit sees 1,120 lb of uplift and weighs 1,400, so at full weight the net is -280, the weight winning -- but ASCE 7's ASD combination counts only 0.6 of the weight (840 lb), and then the WIND wins by 280 lb, adding 35 lb to each windward fastener on top of the overturning couple (corrected 2026-10-01). THE COUPLE IS THE PART THAT GETS OMITTED ENTIRELY and it is frequently the larger demand: lateral wind acts well above the curb and resolves across the width, so a TALL NARROW UNIT IS HARDER TO ANCHOR THAN A LOW WIDE ONE OF THE SAME WEIGHT -- the lever arm grows and the resolving width shrinks together. AND THE LOAD PATH HAS TWO PARTS, THE SECOND INVISIBLE: a unit adequately screwed to a curb that is only nailed to a wood deck fails at the deck, and post-event roof inspections find exactly that.

assumptions.name: Design pressures entered
assumptions.value: for the zone and height the unit actually sits at

assumptions.name: Lateral force at mid-height
assumptions.value: the unit's centroid is assumed at mid-height of the side profile

assumptions.name: Unit-to-curb only
assumptions.value: the curb-to-deck connection is a separate and invisible check
assumptions.source: the curb manufacturer and the roofer
